title: Three-Week IB Design Technology Revision Plan
summary: IB Design Technology revision plan for November: follow a flexible three-week schedule for topic triage, exam practice, timed papers, and proper rest.
body_markdown:
Three weeks can feel uncomfortably short. It is also enough time to make progress if you stop treating every topic as equally urgent.


This IB Design Technology revision plan is for November 2026 candidates balancing several subjects. Diagnose weaknesses in week one, repair priority gaps in week two, and rehearse exam conditions in week three.


November 2026 candidates follow the course with its final assessment in 2026; the revised course is first assessed in 2027. SL includes Papers 1 and 2, while HL includes Papers 1, 2 and 3. Confirm your timetable and assessment arrangements with your school.


### Your three-week plan at a glance


- **Week one:** diagnose weaknesses and rebuild essential knowledge.
- **Week two:** apply knowledge through structured questions.
- **Week three:** complete timed papers, review errors and protect sleep.
- **Every session:** record what went wrong and what happens next.


Try 45-60 minutes on weekdays and a longer weekend block with a break. Shorten sessions when another subject needs attention.


### Before week one: build an honest topic map


Divide your school’s syllabus into three categories: green for topics you can explain and apply, amber for incomplete understanding, and red for material you cannot retrieve confidently.


The six core areas are human factors and ergonomics, resource management and sustainable production, modelling, final production, innovation and design, and classic design. HL students must also map extension content and Paper 3 demands.


Test your categories using the[IB Design Technology Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-design-technology/questionbank) . A familiar page can conceal weak recall. Answering without notes gives you better evidence of readiness.


### Week one: diagnose and rebuild the foundations


Start with a mixed diagnostic set containing short responses, data interpretation and an extended response. HL students should include Paper 3 material. The[IB Design Technology resource library](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-design-technology) brings together questions and revision resources for this work.


Choose no more than three red topics initially. For each, read a focused section of Study Notes, close it, and write the key ideas from memory. Check omissions, then attempt 5-10 targeted questions. Use Flashcards to revisit terminology between longer sessions.


Keep a one-page mistake log. Record causes such as “confused percentile range with average dimensions” or “described sustainability without evaluating trade-offs.” Each entry should tell you what to change next time.


The guidance in[how to get a 7 in IB Design Technology](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-get-a-7-in-design) can help connect knowledge with precise answers. Finish the week by retrying questions you initially struggled with, without looking at your corrections first.


A student presents an overengineered pencil while another asks whether it has improved the answer


### Week two: turn knowledge into marks


Shift time from reading to application. Knowing a definition is useful; selecting it for an unfamiliar product scenario takes additional practice.


Build sessions around connected ideas. Combine ergonomics with user-centred design, or manufacturing choices with environmental impact. Explain how a design decision affects a specific user, producer or stage of the product lifecycle.


Schedule two targeted sessions, one mixed question set and one extended-response session. HL students should reserve additional time for extension content and Paper 3 application. Keep one short review for Flashcards and recurring mistakes.


When checking answers, ask: did I follow the command term, use relevant evidence, and explain my reasoning? For evaluation, identify competing considerations and justify your conclusion in context.


RevisionDojo’s AI Chat can clarify a concept after your own attempt, while Grading tools can highlight answers needing closer review. Compare feedback with teacher guidance. Consult the[common Design Technology exam mistakes guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/top-mistakes-to-avoid-in-ib-design-technology-exams) when scores remain inconsistent.


For collaborative revision, use the[Design Technology study-group guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-design-technology-study-group-fall) to keep meetings focused on testing and discussion.


### Week three: rehearse the exam, then recover


Complete timed papers using the conditions you expect on examination day. Remove notes, silence your phone and observe the permitted time. Practise moving on when a question stalls you, then returning if time remains.


SL students should rehearse Papers 1 and 2; HL students should include Paper 3. Leave enough time between attempts to review and repair errors.


Classify each mistake:


- **Knowledge:** a concept or term was missing.
- **Application:** knowledge was not connected to the scenario.
- **Technique:** the command term or answer structure was mishandled.
- **Timing:** too long was spent on one question.


Use the next session to address the largest category. RevisionDojo’s Predicted Papers and Mock Exams offer further rehearsal; its[exam-style Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) supports focused practice between full attempts. Treat predictions as practice, never as a guarantee of examination content.


Keep the final 48 hours lighter. Review definitions, product examples and your mistake log. Avoid opening several unfamiliar topics at once. Prepare your equipment and confirm examination arrangements.


### Make the plan fit your other subjects


Place examinations, school commitments, sleep and essential coursework into your timetable first. Allocate revision around urgency and demonstrated weaknesses. Design Technology might receive five sessions one week and three the next.


Use RevisionDojo as a connected resource: Study Notes for clarification, Flashcards for retrieval and questions for application. Its Coursework Library and Tutors can support specific needs, although examination preparation should remain your immediate priority. The[Design Technology tools and resources guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/the-best-tools-and-resources-for-ib-design-technology-students) can help you choose resources deliberately.


Protect a regular stopping time and some time away from study. A workable schedule leaves room to recover and adjust when a session takes longer than expected.


### Your next useful action


Begin with one diagnostic set today. Choose three weaknesses, schedule focused practice and reserve time for timed rehearsal. Return to RevisionDojo to test whether your corrections hold without notes. The aim is to enter November with clearer knowledge, fewer recurring errors and a reliable approach to unfamiliar questions.
